At Corgi, we hear this a lot: growing companies stacking up different insurance providers as they scale, and every single one of them a pain to deal with. That's what happened to Tandem. They're an AI-native office leasing agent that's helped more than 250 companies in San Francisco, New York, and Boston find office space, so they know a thing or two about processes that should be simple but aren't. As they built out their business over the past couple of years, they'd had to piece together insurance from a handful of different providers. Every time, it was a hassle. With Corgi: one simple form, an instant quote, insured the same day. Rafi Sands , CEO, Tandem says it himself: "As soon as we hit submit, we had an instant quote and were able to actually find that policy and get insurance as quickly as the same day." ...more ...more

Companies are spending more on AI every month, but almost none of that spending becomes an asset they own. Experiential Labs is changing that. Keep using the models you already use. Experiential Labs uses your traffic to build a simulation of the tasks, failures, and edge cases your agent encounters. The platform trains you a model against that simulation, so it gets better at your specific use cases over time. As your model improves, it earns more of the traffic while the most difficult requests still go to GPT or Claude. On some tasks, they've seen up to 97% lower cost and 50% higher quality. Across a full deployment, they guarantee at least 50% lower cost at the same or better quality, backed by an SLA. Between the founders Kion Fallah and Silen Naihin , they have earned an ML PhD, led an AV simulation team, built the first AI agent with AutoGPT, and published AI research in top conferences. What's your team spending on models you don't own? Reach out to founders@experientiallabs.ai or visit experientiallabs.ai . Congrats on the launch, Kion and Silen! 🚀 https://lnkd.in/gwy-65_B ...more ...more

PRINCEPS (YC S26) is now backed by Y Combinator ! I spent my entire time at Oxford preparing for a world that no longer exists. Universities bred young graduates to become knowledge factories. Education and intelligence were the insurance we placed on our futures. Then the world made intelligence free-flowing. Since the Industrial Revolution, business has carried two great input costs: energy and intelligence. Energy became a utility long ago. Now intelligence is following the same path: no longer rare, no longer locked inside people, but sold by the meter. And on top of it, an entirely new economy is emerging. The agentic economy will run on compute the way the industrial economy ran on power, and compute is now emerging as a mature commodity market. Every asset class before it relied on the same machinery: standards, benchmarks, credit, insurance. PRINCEPS (YC S26) is building the underwriting layer for this new economic future. Huge thanks to Vivian Midha Shen for believing in us. More to follow. En marche. Anya Trofimova , Wilhem Hector PS. If you are in the Bay Area, shoot me a message!
